solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: River Bude winding round one

indicators.note: round means the scrambled town letters go around the other piece
something winding twists about, so the letters of the town name are rearranged

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, meaning one

explanation.surface: A little river meanders around the Cornish resort of Bude.
explanation.walkthrough: Bude is a seaside town in Cornwall, England; 'River' sounds like a local stream, but it is the great European one.
explanation.definitionFit: The Danube is one of Europe's great rivers, flowing from Germany to the Black Sea.

clue.text: Failing to change sides

definitions.meaning: a failing is a shortcoming or flaw
to desert one's cause or country for the opposing one

explanation.surface: Someone failing in their duty switches allegiance.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it means a flaw; as a verb it means to desert to the other side, as a spy or athlete might.

clue.text: Take a letter about Latin film star

parts.note: to nick is to take, as in steal

indicators.note: about means the short letter goes around the abbreviation for Latin

parts.note: a note is a short letter

explanation.surface: Reads like a classroom instruction: take down a letter on the subject of a Latin film star.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick Nolte is an American actor known for 48 Hrs. and The Prince of Tides.
explanation.definitionFit: Nick Nolte is a Hollywood actor, so he is an example of a film star.

clue.text: Supply loot in barrels, for example

definitions.text: Supply loot in barrels, for example

parts.words: Supply loot in barrels, for example
parts.note: pictures the illicit trade in smuggled liquor, sold out of barrels like stolen goods

explanation.walkthrough: The verb means to make, carry or sell alcohol illegally, as in Prohibition-era America; barrels of contraband spirits are the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Illegally trading in spirits is the original sense of the word, from smugglers hiding flasks in their boot tops.

clue.text: Mysterious man after key to boozer

indicators.note: after means the man's name is placed following the other two pieces

parts.note: E is a musical key
a sot is a habitual drunkard
Eric is a man's name

explanation.surface: A shady figure comes looking for the key to the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boozer' suggests a British pub, its slang sense; here it is a heavy drinker instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Something esoteric is understood only by an inner circle, hence obscure or mysterious to outsiders.

clue.text: Appears with good sort of act getting prolonged applause

parts.note: shows up means appears; shows alone can mean appears
a topper is old slang for a fine fellow, a good sort

explanation.surface: A performer turns up with a fine routine that wins long applause.
explanation.definitionFit: A turn in a show so well received that the applause halts the performance is called this.

clue.text: Historian understood by you and me

parts.note: tacit means understood without being said
us is you and me together

explanation.surface: A historian whose meaning is clear to both of us.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacitus was the Roman historian who wrote the Annals and the Histories.

clue.text: Hog's back, a cold place when Fahrenheit's dropped

indicators.note: dropped means the letter for Fahrenheit is removed

parts.note: a fridge is a place kept cold
F is the abbreviation for Fahrenheit

explanation.surface: Pictures a pig's back being chilled, temperature unit and all.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hog's Back is a long chalk ridge in Surrey, England; 'Hog's back' looks like a pig's spine.
explanation.definitionFit: A hog's back is a long narrow hill with a sharp crest, a kind of elevated crest of land.

clue.text: Bond securing a second frame

indicators.note: securing means the bonding material holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: cement is a bond, something that binds

explanation.surface: A bond holding a second frame in place, as in building work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' suggests James Bond; here it is the binding material.
explanation.definitionFit: A casement is a window sash hinged at the side, or the frame holding it.

clue.text: Fine player's agent

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
a player is an actor on stage

explanation.surface: A good actor's agent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine' looks like praise of the player; it is just F.
explanation.definitionFit: A factor is a person who acts on behalf of another, especially a business agent.

clue.text: Admits ciphers must involve New Church

indicators.note: involve means the ciphers wrap around the other pieces

parts.note: codes are ciphers
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone owns up that the secret codes include a new church.
explanation.definitionFit: To concede is to acknowledge or grant something as true, often reluctantly.

clue.text: Tin medals forged for groundhog day

parts.note: a can is a tin container

indicators.note: forged means worked into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Metal medals made for a February festival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tin' wants to join 'medals' as fodder; it is CAN. Groundhog Day is 2 February in North America.
explanation.definitionFit: Candlemas falls on 2 February, the same day as North America's Groundhog Day weather custom.

clue.text: Star — not the morning star, and not the evening star!

definitions.text: Star — not the morning star, and not the evening star!

parts.words: Star — not the morning star, and not the evening star!
parts.note: a celebrity of afternoon performances, neither morning nor evening, is the star meant

explanation.walkthrough: Morning and evening star are names for Venus; the afternoon showing of a play or film gives the star meant.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor adored by audiences, named after the afternoon performance popular with fans.

clue.text: Word describing element of heat

indicators.note: describing, in its sense of drawing round, means the word goes around the element

parts.note: a term is a word
H is the symbol for the element hydrogen

explanation.surface: Looks like a request for a word describing some element of heat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'element' looks like part of the heat; it is hydrogen, H. The definition is the combining form, as in thermal.
explanation.definitionFit: As a prefix or word element, therm- signals warmth, as in thermometer and thermostat, so it means relating to warmth.

clue.text: Amusing poet describing English coastal worker, perhaps

parts.note: light verse or entertainment is amusing

indicators.note: describing, in its sense of drawing round, means the poet goes around the other letter

parts.note: A. E. Housman was the English poet of A Shropshire Lad

explanation.surface: A funny poet writing about an English worker on the coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A keeper of a coastal beacon tower is a worker on the coast, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Weapon child found in county town

indicators.note: found in means the child is put inside the town

parts.note: Matlock is the county town of Derbyshire

explanation.surface: A gun turns up with a child in a county town.
explanation.walkthrough: Matlock is the administrative centre of Derbyshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: A matchlock is an early musket fired by a slow match, so a type of firearm.

clue.text: A bishop's vice, the drink

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
a vice is a sin

explanation.surface: A churchman's weakness is a particular spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Absinthe is a strong green aniseed spirit, the drink of Belle Époque Paris.

clue.text: I grip banknote tightly, showing such a level of stress?

indicators.note: tightly here means drunk, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tense person clutching a note so hard they are at their limit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tightly' looks like how the note is gripped; read as 'tight' meaning drunk, it is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The point at which strain or tension becomes too much for someone is a stress threshold.

clue.text: Number having sly look over angler's accessory

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the pieces read upwards

parts.note: ten is a number
a peek is a sly glance

explanation.surface: A fishing gadget with a number and a furtive glance.
explanation.definitionFit: A keepnet is a net in which an angler keeps caught fish alive in the water.

clue.text: Character of myth, one taken in by another

indicators.note: taken in by means the numeral is placed inside the other figure

parts.note: Icarus is another character of Greek myth, the boy who flew too near the sun
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A mythic figure tricked by another.
explanation.definitionFit: Icarius was a figure in Greek legend, the father of Penelope in some tellings.

clue.text: Religious house in earlier years

parts.note: prior means earlier

explanation.surface: A convent of times gone by.
explanation.definitionFit: A priory is a monastery or nunnery headed by a prior or prioress.

clue.text: Lives next door to woman with children

indicators.note: next door to means the woman's name sits right beside the other piece

parts.note: is means lives or exists
Sue is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A neighbour with kids.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue is a legal word for offspring or descendants.

clue.text: Brush or brushwood?

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means rub hard, as with a brush; as a noun it is stunted vegetation.

clue.text: Attention given to female in pub, incessant talker

parts.note: giving an ear means paying attention

indicators.note: in means the female is put inside the pub

parts.note: a bar is a pub
she is a female pronoun

explanation.surface: A woman at the bar draws attention from a chatterer.
explanation.walkthrough: EARBASHER is British and Australian slang.
explanation.definitionFit: To bash someone's ear is to talk at them at length, so this is a nonstop chatterer.

clue.text: Mournful song Rodney composed on Thursday

indicators.note: on means the rearranged name is attached to the day
composed means put together, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Rodney writes a sad song on a Thursday.
explanation.definitionFit: A threnody is a lament or dirge, a poem or song of mourning.

clue.text: Escort taking carriage to capital, once son's dropped off

parts.note: a gig is a light two-wheeled carriage

indicators.note: dropped off means the letter for son is removed

parts.note: Oslo is the capital of Norway
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A hired companion takes a carriage to the capital after dropping a son.
explanation.definitionFit: A gigolo is a man paid to be a woman's companion or escort.

clue.text: Old PM's back seen first by doctor, to add strength

indicators.note: by means the doctor goes beside that front letter, within the name
the final letter of the statesman's name is shifted to the front

parts.note: Clement Attlee was British Prime Minister 1945-51
MB is a Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor

explanation.surface: An old Prime Minister's back is seen by a doctor before he is strengthened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back seen first' moves Attlee's last E to the front, giving EATTLE; 'by' puts MB next to that E.
explanation.definitionFit: To embattle is to fortify, as with battlements, so to strengthen a position.

clue.text: Has dispersed, essential fruit of a tree

indicators.note: dispersed means scattered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: key means essential or vital

explanation.surface: A vital fruit spread far from its tree.
explanation.definitionFit: An ash key is the winged seed of the ash tree, hanging in bunches.
